name: Looker
description: Looker is Google Cloud's business intelligence and embedded-analytics platform, built around the LookML semantic layer and Gemini-powered Conversational Analytics agents for natural-language querying, dashboarding, and embedding custom data applications.
best_for: Organizations that want a governed, semantic-layer-first BI platform tightly integrated with Google Cloud and BigQuery, and that are comfortable negotiating platform-plus-user pricing with sales rather than buying self-serve.
features: LookML semantic layer that defines business logic and metric definitions once, above the underlying cloud data warehouse
Conversational Analytics: natural-language querying powered by Gemini, including specialized Dashboard Agents embedded directly in BI dashboards
Embedded analytics via Looker APIs and SDKs for building custom data applications and data-to-UI pipelines inside other products
Native integration with Google Cloud, including SSO via Google Cloud IAM, private networking, and direct BigQuery integration
Three per-user license types (Developer, Standard, Viewer) matching cost and capability to how much access each person needs
Data blending for ad hoc analysis of CSVs and local files alongside governed LookML models
pros: Deep native integration with Google Cloud (BigQuery, IAM/SSO, private networking) for teams already on that platform
LookML semantic layer gives one governed, reusable definition of business metrics shared across dashboards, embedded apps, and AI agents
Three distinct user license types (Developer/Standard/Viewer) let organizations match cost to what each person actually needs
cons: No published numeric pricing anywhere — both platform and per-user licensing require an annual commitment and a custom quote from sales
Even the entry Standard edition, meant for teams under 50 users, is priced as 'Call sales' with no self-serve signup or trial pricing shown

pricing.starting_price: No published numeric price; every edition (Standard, Enterprise, Embed) and every per-user license type is priced as a custom quote from Google Cloud sales, under an annual commitment

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.notes: For organizations/teams under 50 users. Includes one production instance, 10 standard users, 2 developer users, upgrades, up to 1,000 query-based API calls/month, and up to 1,000 administrative API calls/month. Annual commitment; priced as 'Call sales'.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: Adds enhanced security features for broader internal BI/analytics use. Includes one production instance, 10 standard users, 2 developer users, upgrades, up to 100,000 query-based API calls/month, and up to 10,000 administrative API calls/month. Annual commitment; priced as 'Call sales'.

tiers.name: Embed
tiers.notes: For deploying and maintaining external analytics and custom applications at scale. Includes one production instance, 10 standard users, 2 developer users, upgrades, up to 500,000 query-based API calls/month, and up to 100,000 administrative API calls/month. Annual commitment; priced as 'Call sales'.

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.description: A Salesforce-owned BI and visualization platform licensed by role (Viewer/Explorer/Creator) with published per-user rates, rather than Looker's contact-sales platform-plus-user pricing.
alternatives.best_for: Teams that want published, self-serve per-role pricing and deep, flexible visual analytics rather than a semantic-layer-first, contact-sales BI platform tied to Google Cloud.
strengths: Dedicated authoring apps for Windows and Mac

alternatives.name: Microsoft Power BI
alternatives.description: Microsoft's BI platform, with simple published per-user pricing and deep integration into Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Fabric, instead of Looker's contact-sales platform-plus-user model.
alternatives.best_for: Organizations already standardized on Microsoft 365 that want low, published per-user BI pricing rather than a contact-sales platform built around Google Cloud and LookML.

faq.question: Is there a free version of Looker?
faq.answer: Google Cloud does not publish a free plan or numeric free-trial terms for Looker (Google Cloud core) — its official pricing page prices every edition as 'Call sales.'

faq.question: How is Looker priced?
faq.answer: Looker pricing has two components: platform pricing (Standard, Enterprise, or Embed edition, each requiring an annual commitment) and per-user licensing (Developer, Standard, or Viewer user types). Every edition and license type is priced as a custom quote from Google Cloud sales — no numeric self-serve rate is published.

faq.question: What's included in the Standard edition?
faq.answer: Standard includes one production instance, 10 standard users, 2 developer users, upgrades, up to 1,000 query-based API calls per month, and up to 1,000 administrative API calls per month, billed under an annual commitment quoted by sales.
